content.introduction: The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) is a unit of the United States Department of Labor, serving as the principal fact-finding agency for the U.S. government in the broad field of labor economics and statistics and a principal agency of the U.S. federal statistical system. The BLS collects, processes, analyzes, and disseminates essential statistical data to the American public, the U.S. Congress, other Federal agencies, state and local governments, businesses, and labor representatives. It conducts a monthly survey of U.S. households, conducted by the United States Census Bureau for the BLS, which provides data on the employed, unemployed, and those not in the labor force, measuring the unemployment rate, labor force participation rate, and employment-to-population ratio. Participation in the survey is voluntary.
